name: Oil pressure warning
means: The engine's oil pressure has dropped too low to protect its moving parts.
why: Low oil level, a failing oil pump, a blocked pick-up, a leak, or a faulty pressure sensor.
drive: No. Stop as soon as it is safe and switch the engine off.
action: Pull off the carriageway and switch off the engine.
Wait a few minutes, then check the oil level with the dipstick on level ground.
If the level is low, top up with the oil grade in your manual and look for leaks.
If the light returns, or the level was fine, do not restart - call for assistance.
ignored: Within minutes, bearings and the camshaft can seize, destroying the engine.
pro: Always, unless topping up to the correct level fixes it and no leak is visible.

name: Coolant temperature warning
why: Low coolant, a leak, a failed fan, a stuck thermostat, a broken water-pump belt or a blocked radiator.
drive: No. Stop safely and switch off.
action: Stop safely and switch off the engine.
Do not open the radiator or expansion-tank cap while hot.
Let the engine cool for at least 30 minutes.
Check the coolant level in the expansion tank; top up only when cold.
Look for leaks or a broken belt. Call for help if unsure.
ignored: A warped cylinder head or blown head gasket - repairs can cost more than the engine is worth.
pro: Yes, unless it was simply low coolant with no leak.

name: Brake system warning
means: The parking brake is on, the brake-fluid level is low, or the braking system has a fault.
why: Parking brake still applied, worn pads lowering the fluid level, a fluid leak, or an EBD fault.
drive: Only if releasing the parking brake turns it off. Otherwise stop and do not drive.
action: Check that the parking brake is fully released.
If the light stays on, stop safely and test the pedal: a soft or sinking pedal is an emergency.
Check the brake-fluid reservoir level.
Do not drive with low fluid or a soft pedal - call for assistance.
ignored: Total or partial loss of braking.
pro: Yes, unless it was only the parking brake.

name: Battery / charging warning
means: The charging system is not charging the battery. The car is running on stored battery power.
why: A broken or slipping alternator belt, a failed alternator, or a loose or corroded battery connection.
drive: Only a short distance to a safe place. The engine may stop when the battery runs flat.
action: Switch off non-essential electrics: AC, music, heated screens.
Drive directly to a safe place or workshop if it is very close.
If the steering becomes heavy or the temperature rises, stop immediately - the same belt may drive the water pump and steering pump.
ignored: The engine will cut out when the battery is drained, possibly in traffic.

name: Power steering warning
means: Power steering assistance has a fault or has been lost.
why: Electric power steering motor or sensor fault, low voltage, or low fluid in hydraulic systems.
drive: Steering still works but can be very heavy. Slow down and stop safely.
action: Hold the wheel firmly with both hands and slow down.
Stop safely, switch off, wait, and restart - some faults reset.
If the steering is still heavy, do not continue; call for assistance.
ignored: Sudden loss of assistance during a turn can cause a crash.

name: Check engine (malfunction indicator)
means: The engine-management system has found a fault that may affect emissions or running.
why: Anything from a loose fuel cap to a failing sensor, misfire or catalytic converter problem.
drive: If steady: yes, carefully, to a workshop soon. If flashing: no - reduce speed and stop safely.
action: Note whether it is steady or flashing and whether the engine runs differently.
If flashing or the engine is shaking, stop and call for help.
If steady and the car drives normally, check the fuel cap and book a diagnostic scan soon.
ignored: Higher fuel use, a failed emissions test, or catalytic converter damage.
pro: Yes - a diagnostic scan reads the stored fault code.

name: ABS warning
means: The anti-lock braking system has a fault and is switched off. Normal brakes still work.
why: A dirty or failed wheel-speed sensor, damaged wiring, or an ABS module fault.
drive: Yes, carefully. Leave bigger gaps - the wheels can lock under hard braking.
action: Drive gently and increase your following distance.
If the red brake light is also on, stop: braking balance may be affected.
Have the system checked soon.
ignored: In an emergency stop the wheels can lock and you lose the ability to steer.

name: Airbag / SRS warning
means: The supplementary restraint system has a fault. Airbags and pretensioners may not work in a crash.
why: A connector under a seat, a clock-spring fault in the steering wheel, a sensor fault, or a previous crash.
drive: The car can be driven, but your crash protection may be reduced. Get it fixed promptly.
action: Make sure everyone wears a seat belt.
Do not try to repair airbag wiring yourself.
Book an inspection soon.
ignored: Airbags may not deploy in a crash, or could deploy unexpectedly.
pro: Always - airbag systems need trained technicians.

name: Tyre pressure (TPMS) warning
means: One or more tyres are significantly below the recommended pressure.
why: A slow puncture, a temperature drop, or a valve leak. A flashing light often means a sensor fault.
drive: Slow down and check as soon as it is safe. Do not drive on a visibly flat tyre.
action: Reduce speed and avoid hard braking.
Stop safely and look at all four tyres.
Inflate to the pressure on the door-pillar sticker at the next opportunity.
If one tyre keeps losing pressure, have it inspected for a puncture.
ignored: Under-inflated tyres overheat and can blow out at speed; handling and braking suffer.
pro: If the pressure keeps dropping or the light flashes.

name: Traction / stability control (ESC)
means: Flashing: the system is actively controlling wheel spin or a skid. Steady: the system is off or has a fault.
why: Flashing on slippery roads is normal. Steady means it was switched off or a sensor has failed.
drive: Flashing: yes, but ease off - you are near the limit of grip. Steady: carefully, and get it checked.
action: If flashing, reduce speed and be smoother with steering and throttle.
If steady, check whether the ESC-off button was pressed.
If it stays on, have it checked.
ignored: You lose protection against skids, especially in the wet.

name: Traction control active
means: The car has detected a driven wheel spinning and is reducing power or braking it.
why: Accelerating on a wet, muddy, sandy or gravel surface.
drive: Yes. Ease off the accelerator and drive more smoothly.
action: Lift slightly off the accelerator.
Pull away in a higher gear on slippery surfaces in a manual car.
ignored: Repeated wheelspin wears tyres and can lead to a skid if traction control is off.
pro: No, unless it lights up on dry roads.

name: Diesel particulate filter (DPF)
means: The diesel particulate filter is getting blocked with soot and needs to clean itself (regenerate).
why: Many short, slow trips that never get the exhaust hot enough to burn the soot off.
drive: Yes. A sustained drive at steady highway speed usually lets it regenerate.
action: Drive for 15–20 minutes at a steady speed on a highway, as your manual describes.
If the light stays on or other warnings join it, book a service.
ignored: The filter can block completely, causing limp mode and an expensive replacement.
pro: If it does not clear after a regeneration drive.

name: Glow plug indicator (diesel)
means: The glow plugs are heating the combustion chambers to help a cold diesel start.
why: Normal at start-up. Flashing while driving usually signals an engine-management fault.
drive: Wait for it to go out before cranking. If it flashes while driving, get it checked.
action: Turn the key to ignition and wait for the light to go out, then start.
If it flashes while driving, treat it like a check-engine light.
ignored: Hard starting and extra wear; a flashing light may hide a real fault.
pro: If it flashes while driving or starting is hard.

name: Immobiliser / key warning
means: The car does not recognise the key, so the engine will not start or may stop after starting.
why: Low key-fob battery, a damaged key chip, a spare key not programmed, or a system fault.
drive: Usually it will not start. If it does, the light should go out within seconds.
action: Try your spare key.
Hold the key fob against the start button or steering column as the manual describes.
Replace the fob battery.
If nothing works, contact an authorised service centre.
ignored: You may be stranded - the car is protecting itself from theft.
pro: If a working spare key also fails.

name: Low fuel warning
means: The fuel tank is nearly empty; the remaining range is limited.
why: Fuel has dropped to the reserve level.
drive: Yes, to the nearest fuel station.
action: Refuel at the next opportunity.
Drive smoothly to stretch the range.
Do not rely on the range estimate on hilly roads.
ignored: Running dry can strand you in a dangerous place and can damage the fuel pump; diesels may need the system bled.

name: Seat belt reminder
means: The driver or a passenger is not wearing a seat belt.
why: A belt is unfastened, or an object on the passenger seat triggers the sensor.
drive: Not until everyone is belted in.
action: Fasten every belt before moving off.
Move heavy bags off the passenger seat.
ignored: Unbelted occupants are far more likely to be killed or seriously injured, and it is an offence.
pro: No, unless a fastened belt still triggers it.

name: Parking brake applied
why: It was not fully released before moving off.
action: Release the parking brake completely.
If the light stays on, check the brake-fluid level - the same light often signals low fluid.
ignored: Overheated rear brakes, worn pads and reduced braking when you need it.
pro: If the light stays on after release.
